title: Cognitive Dissonance Theory Explained
text:
Cognitive dissonance theory, developed by Leon Festinger, proposes that individuals experience psychological discomfort when holding two or more conflicting beliefs, values, or attitudes. This inconsistency creates an internal pressure to reduce the dissonance, often by changing one of the conflicting cognitions or adding new ones to justify the behavior.

The severity of the dissonance is proportional to the importance of the cognitions involved and the degree of discrepancy between them. To alleviate this tension, people frequently employ rationalization, which involves selectively seeking information that supports their current actions or beliefs while ignoring contradictory evidence.
